title: tournament-bracket-eval-summary-oct-2025
summary: Quick decisions memo from the round-robin / bracket-style model onboarding evaluation run in Oct 2025. Goal: pick a candidate to promote to candidate-serving pool for internal smoke tests and hard-regression monitoring. We ran a two-phase tournament: (1) seeded round-robin across 6 model variants, (2) single-elimination bracket among the top 4 by composite score. This doc captures methodology, short results, failure modes, and a recommended next step.
background: We needed a compact, interpretable comparison across many axes (utility, safety, latency, cost) without relying on a single aggregate metric used previously. Bracket format forces head-to-head decision points and surfaced edge-case regressions that leaderboard averages missed. Participants: v2.4-ref, v3.0-base, v3.0-quant8, v3.1-instr, v3.1-small-cache, v3.0-ll-lite. Evaluation window: 2025-10-06 through 2025-10-11. Prompt sets focused on 5 verticals: code-assist, synthesis (longform), summarization (noisy-docs), instruction-following, safety-challenges (adversarial-but-legal).
methodology: High level: For round-robin we sampled 200 seed prompts per vertical, stratified by length and temperature sensitivity. Each pairwise match used head-to-head ranking by three human raters + automated metrics. Human scoring rubric: correctness (0-2), helpfulness (0-2), harm-risk (0-2 where lower is better), hallucination-flag (binary). Automated: BLEU-like match for code, ROUGE-L for summaries, toxicity score (Perspective), latency (p50/p95 measured on k80 and on-prod GPU), tokenized cost estimate using our pricing table. Composite score = weighted sum (human correctness 30%, helpfulness 20%, harm-adjustment 20%, latency-cost combined 20%, automated task metric 10%). We recorded full outputs for regression playback and KV-cache stress tests.
dataset_and_prompt_sets: Prompt sets: code-assist-v2 (200 prompts, includes buggy snippets), long-synth-2025 (200 prompts, 2-5k token contexts), noisy-docs-summarize (200 prompts with OCR-like noise), instr-follow-compact (200 stepwise tasks), safety-adversarial (150 prompts curated by red-team). Notes: we intentionally included 30% prompts with rare tokens and 20% multi-turn contexts to stress KV cache. Prompt templates, seed IDs, and human-rater guidelines are in linked artifact CONFLUENCE- BRKT-2025 and PR 312.
metrics_and_scoring: We tracked per-prompt: human score aggregate, auto-metric, harm-flag rate, latency p50/p95, cost_perk (approx tokens * unit_price), and fail-mode labels. For bracket decisions we used pairwise majority on human aggregate then fallback to composite score delta > 0.05. For ties we used harm-rate then latency as tie-breakers. All metric time-series attached to CONFLUENCE-ML (link above).
results_snapshot: Round-robin top ordering by composite: 1) v3.1-instr, 2) v3.0-base, 3) v3.0-quant8, 4) v2.4-ref, 5) v3.1-small-cache, 6) v3.0-ll-lite. Bracket winners: semifinal (v3.1-instr beat v3.0-quant8), (v3.0-base beat v2.4-ref). Final: v3.1-instr vs v3.0-base: v3.1-instr wins majority (human agg 1.43 vs 1.29) but with slightly higher harm-flag rate (3.1% vs 2.0%) and ~12% higher token cost due to longer completions. Example head-to-head spot summaries below (each line is a condensed head-to-head stat): - v3.1-instr vs v3.0-base: human-win 62%, harm-flags 3.1% vs 2.0%, p95 latency +6ms, cost delta +12% - v3.0-quant8 vs v2.4-ref: human-win 55%, hallucination-rate 1.8% vs 2.4%, p95 latency -18ms, cost -28% - v3.0-base vs v3.0-quant8 (seed match): human-win tie 49/51, but quant8 produced concise answers on long-context summarization where cost delta favored quant8.
bracket_notes: Observability: v3.1-instr produced notably better stepwise instruction adherence on instr-follow-compact but tended to be more verbose on synthesis prompts, inflating cost. v3.0-quant8 shows strong latency and cost wins but occasional truncation/hallucination pattern on multi-turn code-assist followups—likely due to quantization-induced tokenization edge cases. v3.1-small-cache failed KV cache stress test in 8% of sampled long-context prompts (fallbacks generated empty outputs) —root cause tracked in JIRA-ML-5499. v3.0-ll-lite consistently underperforms on safety-adversarial set (harm flags 6.7%) and is excluded from next-stage candidates.
decision_recommendation: Promote v3.1-instr to candidate-serving pool for 2-week smoke + hard-regression testing across Dedicated and Hosted routes, with these guardrails: - Enable safety-layer hard-block for outputs with >=2 high-risk indicators until we tune the model. - Run a production-matched traffic shadow for 48 hours on low-risk tenant and monitor harm-rate and cost drift. - Keep v3.0-quant8 as a parallel cost-optimized candidate for embargoed internal trials (suitable for latency sensitive customers) while we address truncation edge cases. Do NOT promote v3.1-small-cache or v3.0-ll-lite.

open_questions: - Is the verbosity of v3.1-instr fixable via system prompts / decoding knobs or will it require a model reweight? (action: analysis during smoke tests) - How representative are our synthetic safety-adversarial prompts vs production attacks? Consider one-off red-team ramp. - Quantized truncation: local repro exists; do we need a kernel change or can tokenization patch suffice? - SLA/cost trade for customers who need low latency: can quant8 be certified as a lower-tier offering?
